subject: reasoning
question: E, F, G, H, K, L and N are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only two people sit between H and G when counted from the right of H. Only three people sit between L and N when counted from the right of N. G sits to the immediate right of N. K sits to the immediate right of E. How many people sit between F and E when counted from the left of F?
solution:
Given:

E, F, G, H, K, L and N are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

Only three people sit between L and N when counted from the right of N.

G sits to the immediate right of N.

Only two people sit between H and G when counted from the right of H.

K sits to the immediate right of E

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce5012a11ad65185b1b3b8d2bcd2c073f1d033ca151ac073186baece49d0cd7d.png] 

Thus, 3 people sit between F and E when counted from the left of F.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**
